summary: Open arterial-tree geometry exists but only for humans and mostly for large vessels: BraVa (61 subjects, SWC trees of cerebral arteries with morphometrics) and the Awakening ImageCAS centerline graphs with lumen radius (999 coronary trees, CC BY-NC). VMR hosts patient-specific cardiovascular models but its contents could not be counted from static HTML. None tabulates bifurcation angles, none samples the smallest side branches the claim describes, and no non-human arteries were found; TCIA has no vessel collection by name.
next_step: Confirm which morphometrics BraVa exposes (bifurcation angle, radius) by fetching one SWC record, and have VMR's model list enumerated through its site or repository; then pre-register the angle-versus-relative-radius regression restricted to trees with radii at each node.
obstacles_confirmed: Clinical imaging resolves large vessels; smallest-branch angles (70-90 degrees in the claim) are not sampled.
Open trees are human only; no non-human vertebrate arterial tree was found.
